f143r.summary: Mayenne to the King, April 1586, after the capitulation of Castets: its captain, unhappy with the King of Navarre, has agreed to leave him; a treaty of twelve thousand ecus in three months, leave to sell his property and a pardon to be registered by the Parlement. The clear copy is f. 155r.

f143v.summary: The Castets despatch continued, on the terms and the march of the army; the clear copy is f. 155r-v.
f143v.en:
since we have from him this undertaking not to bear arms for his party for six months, where he [l. 26] could have
done [?much more] harm; [l. 27] and I have great hope of drawing him away from it [l. 28]
altogether. In doing so, I hope to be able to [?get] good service [l. 29] from him, and through his means and
example to draw away other [l. 30] men and places of consequence.

That is what [l. 31] moved me to enter into this treaty more willingly.

[l. 32] On which Your Majesty will, if it please you, let me know your [l. 33] intention. I have left the whole
of it, except the sum to which [l. 34] I have pledged my word, subject [l. 35] to the good pleasure of […].

(Pour beaucoup davantaige: "by a good deal more"; the f. 155v copy has pour beaucoup davantage. The closing figures stand where the copy has Vostre Majesté, "Your Majesty", but
they do not spell it.)

Yesterday(?)

f150r.summary: Forget to Villeroy, April 1586, on how the composition of Castets was made: 'if there was a fault in the substance, there was more in the form'. The clear copy is f. 155v.

f150.summary: The same letter continued: the two commanders listen too readily to their own people, who want no company of one another; Forget thinks he has earned his wages. The clear copy is f. 156r.

f154.summary: Forget to Villeroy after Easter 1586: the pay of two musters owed, captains' complaints, and lenders who had promised money to be repaid in Paris drawing back; forty thousand ecus. The clear copy is f. 157r.

f154v.summary: The same letter continued in two cipher blocks: Villeroy's advice to raise money on exchange, and the difficulty of doing it at Bordeaux. Clear copy f. 157r.

f173.summary: To the King, 1586: the credit crisis; no means to pay two musters, the town refuses to contribute on the strength of the King's letters, no one will stand surety, and only merchants of Paris lend on the writer's word.
f173.en:
Sire, Your Majesty has been sufficiently informed by the last two despatches of Monsieur du Mayne

[l. 1] […] [44] of the extreme necessity in [?which] [l. 2] he [?finds] himself, seeing himself cheated of the
arrival [l. 3] of the third month, which for more than six weeks [l. 4] he thought to be on the road.

And having [l. 5] no means of paying the men of [?war] [l. 6] for the two musters he has been forced to [?have them]
[l. 7] make, for which he is pressed with [l. 8] […] harshness and disrespect [?unheard of], [l. 9] for which he has
found no other remedy than to send me back […] [l. 10] for the second time, both to beg those [l. 11] of the
[?body] of this town to […] be willing to [?help] [l. 12] in this business, and to try to raise [l. 13] money on his
bonds, at whatever interest [l. 14] it might be.

f196.summary: To the King, 1586, 'Depuis le partement du S.r de Bosseval': a siege report naming Sainct-Chamarand, la Barge, Montberault and la Binault, Mayenne's fever, Marshal Matignon pressed to come, two trenches and a battery of fifteen cannon.

f201.summary: The same despatch as f. 196, enciphered again with different homophones and with more of it in clear; the two were aligned figure by figure.

f196v.summary: The continuation of the ff. 196/201 despatch, dated in clear 'Du camp devant Monségur ce [...] jour de May 1586': the siege of Monségur, a battery of fifteen cannon to open the day after tomorrow, the defenders resolved to hold out after Navarre's treatment of the commander of Sainte-Bazeille, Navarre leaving for Saintonge to meet his reiters while Turenne holds the province from Nérac, the army short of money and the third month's pay.
f196v.en:
[f. 196r ends: However, because the town is large and hard to besiege, it has been necessary to dig]
[l. 1] trenches in several places. And being [l. 2] short of pioneers, the work has [l. 3] been the longer for it.

I believe that the day after tomorrow we shall [l. 4] begin to batter it with a battery of fifteen cannon, at
which [l. 5] it seems likely they will be taken aback, not being [l. 6] used to seeing places besieged in [l. 7] this
country with such an equipage.

Nevertheless, so far they [l. 8] make every show of wishing to [l. 9] defend themselves, so as not to suffer the
shame that the King of Navarre made [l. 10] the man who commanded in Sainte- [l. 11] Bazeille suffer, whom it is
certain he has had [l. 12] put in prison.

And if it is said that he means [l. 13] to do to him pas […] (the sentence breaks off: faire pas and then the
next sentence;

f123r.summary: Mayenne to the King from Marmande, March 1586, opening in clear ('la dernière que j'ay eu l'honneur est du huictiesme de ce moys'): no money, contributions to be had only by garrisons, the troops cannot be kept together.

f123v.summary: The Marmande despatch continued: Turenne back over the Garonne, the relief of places, the army's wants.

f124r.summary: The Marmande despatch continued: the bearer sent to learn the King's intention.

f124v.summary: The end of the Marmande despatch.

f110.summary: Mayenne to Villeroy from Villeneuve-d'Agenais, March 1586: on making war without money and what it does to his reputation; the leaf is wholly in cipher.
f110.en:
[l. 1] [?Sir], [?Villeroy],

you will see well by the letter that I am writing to the King […] [l. 2] […] [?held back] from […] the most […]
that I […] [l. 3] [?reserved] about [?speaking] more freely with you, with what (he) had always made [l. 4]
[?much] of the great [?confidence] and particular friendship, (which) I [?recognised] [l. 5] from the beginning.

For the little […] that I have seen this [l. 6] army have, that it was of little [?consideration], and that one
did not expect [l. 7] much good effect from it, […] more particularly remarked in that [l. 8] passage which is in
your last despatch, that the King has taken […] [l. 9] the dangers that befall those who undertake war without
money.

[l. 10] As he has done […] [45]-ment, that [47] […] words, he has had […] [l. 11] no more substance.

Restraint appears from it. One must speak plainly.

fr15571-f177.summary: Forget, 31 December 1585, on Mayenne's design for Gascony: a plan on Pons and Taillebourg, with Taillebourg's toll on the Charente and thirty thousand ecus to be raised from the country, given up when the vicomte de Turenne took the field with guns. The verso (11 lines) continues it.
fr15571-f177.en:
[l. 1] … besieging Pons and Taillebourg, which it was [l. 2] said could be done both together, and that [l. 3]
beyond doubt we would carry [l. 4] them; and that this would have been for the enemy, [l. 5] especially as regards
Taillebourg, the loss of a [l. 6] great revenue that they draw from the crossing [l. 7] of the Charente, where they
levy [l. 8] heavy dues, and would restore the King to the [l. 9] enjoyment of the taille of all this [?country],
[l. 10] which is said to come to a great deal.

That besides this the country [l. 11] offered us thirty thousand écus to help [l. 12] with the cost of the siege.

And being [l. 13] already so disposed that we agreed that, [l. 14] if news came of some [?stirring] in
Guyenne, [l. 15] Monsieur the Marshal de Matignon [l. 16] would go there with some few [?forces] to [l. 17]
[?oppose] it, and also prepare what would be [l.

f20r.summary: Mayenne to the King, January 1586 (endorsed 'Mr du Mayne du vjme Januier 1586'), the end of the f. 18 despatch: the remains of four regiments and Colonel Heid's Swiss to meet again on the 6th of next month; he will not be drawn into the Limousin and Quercy, since intercepted letters of Turenne to the King of Navarre show Tulle about to compound for four or five thousand ecus and Lamorez to withdraw to Navarre.
f20r.en:
> Translation by Michael Brackx (issue #87, 23 Oct 2026), with the same holes as the copy.

The remains of the regiments of [?Sacremore], of [?Vic], of [?] [?] and of la Roche [?Montoisy], and that of the
Swiss of Colonel Heid. We have fixed a day to meet again on the [?6th] of next month, resolved not to stop at any
enterprise unless it is [?very] easy, since [?it] would be a shame for the negligence. Several of those on this side
would like to draw me into the Limousin and the Quercy, but I see that this would make me spend too much time, having
also learnt from some intercepted letters of the vicomte de Turenne to the King of Navarre that they are about to come
to terms to get the garrison out of Tulle, for four or five thousand écus that the people of the said town ask;

system: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
